newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks MPs bring scandal truckload to parliament.
newsitem.headline: Turks MPs bring scandal truckload to parliament.

text.p: Turkish opposition MPs brought a truckload of petitions to parliament on Wednesday in protest at a scandal over alleged links between leading government officials and far-right gangsters.
The truck, marked with the words "Clean Society", drove to the gates of parliament where some 60 main opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) deputies carried sacks of petititions to the speakers office.
The scandal emerged last month when a truck collided in a fatal crash with a car carrying a government MP, a gangster wanted for murder and a senior policeman.

ANAP deputies said the signatures on the petitions -- which called for changing laws to make it easier to prosecute MPs -- represented only a fraction of the seven million signatures they gathered. ANAP received 5.4 million votes in last year's general elections.
The media has since alleged that Turkey used groups of common criminals for political killings in return for ignoring their heroin-smuggling activities.

ANAP leader Mesut Yilmaz has spearheaded accusations that leading officials, particulalry Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller, are deeply embroiled in the scandal that last month forced the resignation of the interior minister.
